claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a heavy amount of reading required to understand the combat mechanics and character units.

citations.review_text:
I started on mobile near the beginning of Season 7 and recently switched to PC. I play Limbus Company primarily to experience the story. This is also my very first Steam review. I'll get it out of the way that the Steam experience is wonderfully smooth compared to mobile, and I'm glad I decided to switch before experiencing the main boss fight of Canto 8.

[h3]Gameplay and Gacha[/h3]
"Win Rate" memes aside, I like that as long as I respect the boss and enemy mechanics, the enemies in each Canto (how Limbus Company refers to its story chapters) are simple to defeat. The game's currency system also allows you to collect the latest Identities (gacha versions of the playable characters) without spending on in-game currency; I'm only missing four of the current season's House of Spiders Identities despite taking long breaks from the game. Aside from progressing the Limbus Pass and making efficient use of your Enkephalin (energy resource), there's little pressure to log in daily as a casual player, and I was able to complete this season's Limbus Pass even with my breaks.

[h3]Story and Immersive Elements[/h3]
I've not played Lobotomy Corporation or Library of Ruina, so my judgement of the story mainly comes from familiarity with some of the referenced material such as Meursault and Crime and Punishment. The writers behind Project Moon went beyond simply pulling aesthetics and themes from the stories and have interwoven their own interpretations into the namesake characters, their environments, and their growth as Sinners. My favorite so far is Don Quixote, and I'm looking forward to completing Ryōshū's arc.

Korean voice acting as the only option hasn't impacted my experience, though I also have some basic conversational ability. I'm regularly impressed by the English localization as someone who has grown used to some of the quirks of gacha localization, and I enjoy that the Sinners' personalities are so distinct I can easily tell who's speaking with the Enkephali…

HOLY ARTSTYLE
HOLY WORLDBUILDING
HOLY POWERSYSTEM

i still don't know how any of the combat works

More people need to know about this game AND MORE ADVERTISING NEEDS TO BE DONE. YOU HEAR ME KJH. Anyways, for a gacha, it's really free to play friendly, the pity system hurts but technically if you grind enough you wouldn't need to do a single pull. Though I will say there's a lot of reading required to understand the combat and how to use the Identities (units). Also it runs fairly smoothly with my potato ass laptop

citations.review_text: You play as a Manager guiding a crew of Sinners through Dante's Inferno, and the writing does a great job making you care about a cast that starts off pretty unlikeable. Combat is turn-based but tense, with a rock-paper-scissors coin system that punishes autopilot. Story delivery can be text-heavy and the gacha layer is there if you're into that, but the core game underneath is genuinely great. Worth it if you like dark fantasy with real narrative weight behind it.

I've only been playing for a week, but this is probably my favorite gatcha game ever. The story is very well written (It gets quite dark, so be ready for that), the characters have interesting personalities and there is a lot to bring you back each day. The combat is really unique and well made. Its really nice to have combat like this compaired to the generic combat most gatcha games have these days. I highly recommend this game to anyone who wants a fun and unique experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that characters and identities can be acquired entirely for free through a sharding mechanic using currency obtained from mirror dungeons, without needing to engage with the gacha pulls.

citations.review_text:
Its free and you can beat all of the main story without base IDs and you can get all IDs in game without pulling the gatcha once. Great story, great music and you don't need to have played the previous two games to understand the broad strokes of the story. If you are still on the fence then I'll say for the second time that the game is free.

Speaking of the gatcha you get between two to four pulls for free per event and a pull a week from doing daily and weekly missions. IDs are only exclusive to the gatcha for one week after their release) and can be bought with upgrade currency afterwards. The only exceptions are walpurgisnacht IDs and they can be bought at the start of the next event.

absolute peam/
the gameplay generally might be not for everyone, but i will say that the gacha elements are generally forgivable since the game isn't that hard when you pull an id out of the banner (enough to get you through the story if you pull a few good ones), and if you want a specific id then you can get any one you want for shard crates that are easily obtainable from completing mirror dungeons (about 100-200 crates per 000 depending on how many shards you already have on them, +25 about crates if you want to get one to uptie 4)

The story and lore is amazing, so much that at least 3 of the chapters (AKA Canto(s) ) made me cry from how beautifully the story-line was executed. Gameplay may be a little difficult to understand on the first time playing, but more you progress in the game, the more you will understand the gameplay. The gacha system is well overall. 1x and 10x pulls aren't too pricey when compared to the other gacha games I have played. There are different gamemodes you can play to get extra game curreny, the game is pretty F2P friendly. You can also get ID and EGOs by "sharding" for them which doesn't require lunacy like you use for the the gacha system. Maybe some if you're recharging energy, AKA Enkephalin. If you want to know the lore more in depth and/or in chronological order, I suggest you play the games in the order of LobotomyCorporation > Library of Ruina > Limbus Company. Though you won't be shot if you play it out of order, don't worry.

Glory to KJH and Glory to Limbus Company.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the early chapters of the story and the initial gameplay pacing as slow, boring, or confusing for new players.

citations.review_text:
After 100 hours of gameplay, I can't in my good conscience recommend this game to anyone. 

Yes the story is decent, however, it's a slow burn in the early chapters and it drags on more than it hits. The main highlight of the story is how the dynamics between the Sinners change as the story progresses, but this alone can't carry the game in my opinion. If you're here only for the story - just go read a book.

This game has a very complex and intriguing combat system that unfortunately doesn't get used for more than half of the game. You will spend about 50+ hours of your playtime pressing P + Enter instead of using this complex combat system ProjectMoon has created. It's almost like they don't want you to play the game. 

As a final note the descriptions; the descriptions of newer IDs' kits are made so unnecessarily long and key features of an ID's kit are so well hidden somewhere in the "passives" essays, that you may start to think the developers don't really want you to understand what these characters do (maybe that's why P + Enter exists?) My advice is: don't even try, just watch a guide. When you really look at it most of these kits boil down to parries before and after skills and that's all there is to it.

Do not sink your time into this game. It's not worth it as of August 2026,

[b]TLDR (this is a long review)[/b]
- Exceptional story, characters, and worldbuilding, the best I've seen in any game
- However, the early story has bad pacing and is confusing for new players
- Strategic gameplay that can feel immensely rewarding, but confusing to learn and sometimes repetitive
- Beautiful art and stunning animations, though they can sometimes be overwhelming (especially screen shake) 
- Amazing sound design and phenomenal soundtrack (especially Mili), my favourite game soundtrack
- However, endgame is extremely lacking, tedious, and repetitive
- Overall, 9.5/10, would be 10/10 if there was more endgame content



After over 600 hours on Limbus, I can wholeheartedly say that I recommend this game. Despite the flaws that it may have, I still love this game and finally decided to express all of my appreciation here. This is my own take on Limbus Company, the third game of Project Moon’s trilogy, and the points where I believe it shines or could be better.


[b]Story/Characters[/b]
While the gameplay can be fun and rewarding, the story and characters are undoubtedly the reason why this game means so much to me (and to most players). The story is about 13 Sinners who are forced to confront their past and their shortcomings, ultimately leading them to change, no matter how long it may take.

The writing in this game is certainly one of the best I’ve seen. Every Sinner has deep characterisation and a unique personality that make them instantly recognisable; even Dante, the self-insert main protagonist, has their own character, makes mistakes, and grows with the rest of the cast. Even better, the vast majority of story content has voice acting, and while it is only in Korean, the voice actors always make an outstanding performance. From average interactions and funny lines to solemn monologues and emotional outbursts, the voice acting makes each character feel even more authentic.

As for the pacing of the story, it does admittedly start out rough. The f…

I have sunk an unreasonable amount of time into this and I will continue to until the end of this game's lifespan, but I wholeheartedly do not recommend playing this, especially as your first Project Moon game

There are many positives; the story is generally great all the way through, there's a character for almost every type of person, the Sinners all become extremely likeable, and this game's presentation through VFX and sound design are impeccable. This game also has the perk of being worked on by a small and passionate studio with an equally passionate director. It's obvious that everyone working on this deeply cares for what they're making, and I will forever respect that

That's where my compliments end, though. The gameplay is a slog and a general step down in every conceivable way from the previous Library of Ruina-- main story gameplay is boring to get through and challenge content is either difficult in the most unfun possible way or borderline unfair through gating team compositions. Canto 9 has been a general step up in terms of gameplay; it's more akin to how Ruina did fights, and I'm really hoping they keep on that track for Canto X. However, in order to get to Canto 9 in the first place, you have to go through around 30-70 hours of the most mind-numbingly boring gameplay conceived

Balancing suffers from the common insidious killer: powercreep. The power difference between something from seasons 1-3 and seasons 5-7 is genuinely laughable. Some IDs are so braindead busted that they have completely broken team composition and Mirror Dungeon grinding (in which the latter is actually very cool because Mirror Dungeons suck)

The story, while great on its own, is nowhere near the same quality as the previous two Project Moon games thus far. Characters are overall less developed and less interesting in terms of personality, mindsets, and motives (with a few sole exceptions). I do say thus far since this is a live-service game, which brings me to my most maj…

Alright currently I'm typing this out right after finishing canto 9 and I have to say that this game is absolutely fantastic.

It's story is one of the best story's I've ever seen with the characters being well written, the world being fleshed out and the overall plot being genuinely being really interesting. It's gameplay isn't a slouch either with its gameplay being simple enough to learn pretty easily but still having a bit of a learning curve.

And even the gacha mechanics are pretty alright too, with them giving out free currency pretty frequently and the whole sharding mechanic being pretty convenient to utilize. I know that Project Moon gets glazed quite frequently, but quite a lot of that praise is deserved (At least in my opinion).

But yeah if you're thinking about playing limbus I could not recommend it enough, just make sure to give it some time to cook (Canto 1 & 2 can be somewhat boring) but even then they're really not half bad. Well anyway just wanted to share my thoughts about this great game, Glory to Project Moon!

I personally love Limbus Company. The game's story is amazing, the gacha system isn't bad, the gameplay is winrate, and the character design and development great. The only problem is that I feel like there isn't enough publicity from Project Moon itself. Yes it's gotten better but I feel like there isn't enough publicity from Project Moon itself in the U.S. which is unfortunate because the games made by Project Moon are great and deserve more attention.

Some thoughts of mine. The story is great! I'd say it gets interesting at around Canto 4. You can winrate spam up until a certain boss in Canto 4. After that, you kind of have to use your brain. The gameplay can be confusing at first but the most basic thing to understand is that the bigger the number, the better (while also taking into account SP). Everything else? You either learn it as you go along or you ask for help. I did both.
